This appeal is by the claimants who are the parents of deceased, Sri.Sangappa.

The appellants' claim petition in MVC No.1402/2015 on the file of the Senior Civil Judge and MACT-VIII, Muddebihal (for short, the Tribunal) is decided by the judgment and award dated 28.06.2019 awarding a total sum of 14,67,401/- along with interest at the rate of 9% per annum.

sentences.text: The parties, for reasons of convenience, are referred to as the Claimants and Insruer, and at the very outset, this Court must record that there is no dispute that Sri. Sangappa, who was employee an with M/s. Agila Specialties Private Limited, a private enterprise having its Corporate Office at Bannerghatta Road, Bengaluru has died in a road accident on 23.03.2015 when he was traveling on the pillion of Sri. Hampayya who was riding the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.36/EF-6694.
This accident is near Maganoor Village on Hyderabad State Highway.
The Tribunal has absolved the Insurer [the second respondent] of its liability to pay compensation, in the light of its defence that Sri. Hampayya did not have a valid license.

3. In fact, the Tribunal has absolved the Insurer, in the light of the evidence brought on record that with the NC: 2023:KHC-K:5432-DB charge-sheet being filed against Sri. Hampayya for riding the motor cycle without a valid driving license, a notice issued to him by the Insurer to file a copy of his license and this legal notice is returned un-served.

The Tribunal has also found that the claimants,
who were aware of the issuance of the notice, should have taken some action to bring on record the details of the license held by Sri. Hampayya.
4. The claimants first grievance stems from this finding.
The appellants' other grievance is because of the quantum of compensation, and more specifically, the determination of loss of dependency.
The claimants are aggrieved by the annual income that is taken by the Tribunal to determine the loss of dependency but are not aggrieved by the multiplier or deduction towards personal expenses.
Further, the appellants are aggrieved because, though a total sum of Rs.30,000/- is awarded under conventional heads, no amount towards loss of consortium.
5. The learned counsels for the parties are heard and the records are perused in the light of this dispute.

Sri. NC: 2023:KHC-K:5432-DB Hampayya, who admittedly was riding the subject motor cycle at the time of the accident, has chosen to remain absent not just before the Tribunal but also in the present appeal, and crucially he has not responded to the notice issued by the Insurer to produce the details of his license.
This would indicate that the Insurer has brought on record circumstances that could justify a conclusion that Sri. Hampayya did not hold a valid license.
However, this cannot in any manner absolve the Insurer of its liability to pay compensation to the claimants as Sri.Sangappa, who was on the pillion, would be a third party.
The Insurer must therefore pay just and reasonable compensation that is determined and recover the same from Sri.Hampayya in the manner known to law.
6. The claimants, to establish the income of the deceased Sri. Sangappa, have placed on record Ex.P8 and Ex.P10.

The exhibit in Ex.P8 is a Certificate issued by M/s.Agila Specialities Private Limited affirming that Sri.Sangappa is promoted as Operator Grade 'A' with total NC:
2023:KHC-K:5432-DB compensation of Rs.7,700/-.The next document [Ex.P10] is a pay-slip issued for the period from 01.01.2013 to 31.01.2015.

This document indicates, that apart from the sum of Rs.7,700/- indicated in Ex.P8, he was paid certain allowances, and the details of these allowances are:

sentences.text: It is seen from the second column in this Certificate, a sum of Rs.12,700/- is deducted towards staff advance.
It would stand to reason if this Court opines that a sum of Rs.12,700/- shown as other additions is an amount that is received as and advance and is therefore deducted as staff deduction.
In that event, this sum of Rs.12,700/- cannot be part of the income.
7. It is trite that allowances must be treated as part of salary except insofar as those allowances which are treated as re-imbursement of personal expenses of a deceased.

In the NC:
2023:KHC-K:5432-DB present case, where Sri. Sangappa's employment is shown with M/s Agila Specialties Private Limited and his service could be required by the employer in shifts, none of the allowances [other than Rs.12,700/-] can be treated as allowances towards personal expenditure.
As such, the monthly income should be taken as Rs.14,809/- with the necessary additions towards future prospects, and just amount towards consortium.
Of course, there must be deduction at the rate of Rs.150/- towards professional tax as mentioned in Ex.P10.
The addition towards future prospects must be 50% because Sri. Sangappa was in employment with a fixed salary.
The loss of dependency thus computed would be Rs.22,63,482/-.
